event: Checking whether any test covers the hwclr-on-release and CMD_BUSY items, then I'll submit.

I submitted the verdict as "verified", but only 2 of the 5 items actually stand. The other 3 are withdrawn because I found tests that check them.

| Item | Outcome | Why |
|---|---|---|
| CMD_BUSY means the command is not yet complete | Verified (untested) | No test writes CMD_BUSY and checks the busy behavior. The ownership-flow status loop in `mci_mbox_ownership_flow.svh` runs from DATA_READY to CMD_FAILURE and never drives it. |
| `status` hwclr | Withdrawn | `smoke_test_mbox_csr_zeros_after_release.c` writes CMD_STATUS, releases the mailbox, and fails if CMD_STATUS doesn't read 0. |
| `precedence=hw` on simultaneous updates | Verified (untested) | No test makes a hardware clear and a software write land in the same cycle. |
| `swwe=valid_root_req` | Withdrawn | `cptra_smoke_test_mcu_mbox_valid_user.c` has a non-root agent write CMD_STATUS and fails if the value changed. The root write path is exercised in `smoke_test_mcu_mbox_valid_user.c`. |
| `sram_owner` NONE means no owner | Withdrawn | The ownership flow checks that `sram_owner` reads NONE after release (`mci_mbox_ownership_flow.svh:95`). |

**Suggested fix:** add a test that writes CMD_BUSY as root and checks the SRAM ownership handoff doesn't happen. Add a second test that forces a software write to CMD_STATUS in the same cycle as a release, to check that hw wins.
